script.analysis: All 19,773 stored characters read in two contiguous ranges with canonical hash match. Hook: late-night retirement-app comfort vs a quiet "3%" forecast; subscribe framing. Characters Daniel (57, near retirement) and Catherine (28, expects 10-12%). Goldman late-2024 forecast (~3% annualized, 72% probability of trailing bonds, ~1 in 3 of trailing inflation), other firms' lower expectations, Berkshire cash pile, CAPE ~17 average and Buffett indicator, $100K at 10/7/3% over 10 years, Magnificent Seven concentration (~a third), 2022 drawdowns, Natixis expectation gap (~15% vs ~7%), Dalbar behavior gap, sequence risk with 2000-2009 lost decade and Japan 1989-2024, mid-late community CTA and disclaimer, fair bull case (profitable megacaps vs dot-com, AI productivity, valuation warnings that failed in 2017-2021), action: diversify (equal-weight, international, value, bonds), Daniel's safe bucket, Catherine keeps buying; close and second CTA. Balanced and well-sourced core; vague in places ("we've seen the same volatility through '25"). ASR not audio-verified.

claim_audit: 0:9900 Goldman Sachs (Oct 2024) projected ~3% annualized nominal S&P 500 returns for the next decade, ~72% probability of underperforming bonds and ~33% of trailing inflation - consistent with widely reported note; "Just gave" overstates recency (published ~20 months earlier). Vanguard/JPMorgan below-history US equity outlooks consistent. Berkshire's record cash pile consistent with 2024-2025 reports. CAPE long-run ~17 consistent. $100,000 for 10 years at 10%/7%/3% = ~$259K/~$197K/~$134K, gap ~$62-63K - correct. Magnificent Seven roughly a third of the S&P 500 and ~40% 2022 declines vs ~-19% index consistent.

9900:19773 Natixis surveys reported individual investors expecting ~15%+ real returns versus professionals far lower (~7%) - consistent with published survey framing. S&P 500 2000-2009 roughly -1%/year total return - correct. Nikkei 1989 peak regained in early 2024 (~34 years) - correct. Dalbar behavior gap characterized correctly. Bull-case points (megacap profitability vs dot-com, valuation warnings that missed gains 2017-2021, CAPE as long-horizon not timing tool) are fair. Equal-weight, international, value and bond diversification suggestions are generic and reasonable.
